headline: Windows 95 shipped in August, a bomb killed 168 people in Oklahoma City in April, and Rabin was shot in November
texture: The Sampoong Department Store in the Seocho-gu district of Seoul came down on June 29, killing 502 people and injuring 937. A fire in the Baku Metro on October 28 killed 289 passengers. An avalanche buried part of Flateyri in Iceland on October 26 and killed 20, the second one in Iceland that year, and Typhoon Angela left 882 dead in the Philippines and Vietnam on November 7. American Airlines Flight 965 flew into a mountain near Buga in Valle del Cauca on December 20, killing 160 of the 164 aboard.

On February 23 the Dow closed at 4,003.33, and on November 21 at 5,023.55, two millennium marks inside one year. Denver International Airport opened on February 27 as Stapleton shut. Mississippi ratified the Thirteenth Amendment on March 16, the last state to ratify it. Shawn Nelson stole an M60A3 tank from a National Guard armory and drove it through San Diego on May 17. Clinton shut part of Pennsylvania Avenue by the White House to vehicles on May 20, and the Korean War Veterans Memorial was dedicated on July 27.

Andrew Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem appeared in the Annals of Mathematics in May. Valeri Polyakov came back from Mir on March 22 with 438 days in space behind him, and Norman Thagard became the first American to ride up on a Russian launch vehicle, on March 14. Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp each found the same comet on July 23. The Big Ear at the Ohio State University Radio Observatory ended a search for extraterrestrial radio signals it had run continuously for 22 years, and the last signal from Pioneer 11 reached NASA on November 1.

Michel Sardou started a run of 113 shows at the Paris Olympia on January 10. Roxette played to 12,000 people in Beijing on February 19, the first Western band let into the Workers' Indoor Arena in ten years. Def Leppard entered the Guinness Book of World Records on October 23 by playing Tangier, London and Vancouver on one day. Steve Fossett landed a balloon at Leader in Saskatchewan on February 21 after crossing the Pacific alone. Aung San Suu Kyi walked out of house arrest on July 10.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: Al Gore was Vice President and William Rehnquist Chief Justice. Tom Foley was Speaker of the House until January 3 and Newt Gingrich from January 4. George J. Mitchell was Senate majority leader until January 3 and Bob Dole from that day. Robert Rubin was sworn in as Secretary of the Treasury on January 11, succeeding Lloyd Bentsen. Clinton gave the State of the Union address on January 24.

pol.republican_congress.label: Republicans take both houses of Congress
pol.republican_congress.value: The 104th Congress convened, the first controlled by Republicans in both houses since the two years from 1953 to 1955
pol.republican_congress.detail: The House passed a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution by 300 votes to 132 on January 26, and the Senate voted an amendment down by one vote on March 2. The House voted 246 to 188 on April 5 to cut taxes for individuals and corporations, and House Republicans celebrated the passage of most of the Contract with America on April 7. The House passed the Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act on November 1.

pol.oklahoma_city.label: Oklahoma City bombing
pol.oklahoma_city.value: A bomb set off by Timothy McVeigh at the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building killed 168 people, including eight federal marshals and 19 children, and wounded 680
pol.oklahoma_city.detail: The year page calls it the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in United States history and names Terry Nichols as an accomplice. Clinton visited the city on April 23 and told the crowd that today our nation is joined with you in grief. What was left of the building was demolished on May 23. Clinton closed part of Pennsylvania Avenue in front of the White House to traffic on May 20 in response to the bombing.

pol.government_shutdown.label: Federal government shuts down twice
pol.government_shutdown.value: A budget standoff between Democrats and Republicans in Congress closed the federal government from November 14 to 19, and a second shutdown began on December 16
pol.government_shutdown.detail: The US year page dates the reopening of the second shutdown to a day in the following year, so no end date is given here.

pol.mexico_loan.label: Emergency loan to Mexico
pol.mexico_loan.value: Clinton invoked emergency powers to extend a $20 billion loan to help Mexico avert financial collapse
pol.mexico_loan.detail: The year page files the same day under the Mexican peso crisis.

world.rabin.label: Yitzhak Rabin assassinated
world.rabin.value: The Israeli prime minister was shot at a peace rally in Tel Aviv
world.rabin.detail: The year page carries the killing in one line, with no gunman named, no reaction and no successor.

world.bosnia.label: Srebrenica massacre and the end of the Bosnian War
world.bosnia.value: Units of the Army of Republika Srpska under General Ratko Mladic entered Srebrenica against little resistance from Dutch peacekeepers of the United Nations Protection Force and went on to kill thousands of Bosniak men and boys and rape many women
world.bosnia.detail: Twenty-one Bosnian Serb commanders had been charged with genocide and crimes against humanity on February 13. NATO began Operation Deliberate Force against Bosnian Serb artillery on August 30. A United Nations tribunal charged Radovan Karadzic and Mladic with genocide on November 16. Talks opened at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base near Dayton, Ohio on November 1, the Dayton Agreement was reached there on November 21 and signed in Paris on December 14, and NATO began peacekeeping in Bosnia on December 20.

world.kobe.label: Great Hanshin earthquake
world.kobe.value: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck southern Hyogo Prefecture in Japan with a maximum Shindo of 7, leaving between 5,502 and 6,434 people dead
world.kobe.detail: The year page gives the displaced as between 251,301 and 310,000 and cites statistics published by the City of Kobe. Its own image caption rounds the toll to over 6,000, which is the top of the range the text gives rather than a separate figure.

world.tokyo_sarin.label: Tokyo subway sarin attack
world.tokyo_sarin.value: Members of the doomsday cult Aum Shinrikyo released sarin on the subway, killing 14 people and injuring over a thousand
world.tokyo_sarin.detail: Japanese police besieged the cult's headquarters near Mount Fuji on May 16 and arrested its leader Shoko Asahara. Further operations brought over two hundred arrests, and thirteen members including Asahara were sentenced to death.

world.wto.label: World Trade Organization established
world.wto.value: The WTO replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

world.eu_enlargement.label: Austria, Finland and Sweden join the European Union
world.eu_enlargement.value: The three countries entered on the first day of the year
world.eu_enlargement.detail: The Schengen Agreement, which the year page says eased cross-border travel, took effect in several European countries on March 26. Twenty-seven nations signed the Barcelona Treaty on November 28, creating the Union for the Mediterranean. The European Parliament elected its first European Ombudsman, Jacob Soderman, in September.

world.barings.label: Barings Bank collapses
world.barings.value: The United Kingdom's oldest investment banking firm failed after the securities broker Nick Leeson lost $1.4 billion speculating on the Tokyo Stock Exchange

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, worldwide
value: Die Hard with a Vengeance, $366,101,666, 20th Century Fox
Toy Story, $361,958,736, Walt Disney Pictures
Apollo 13, $355,237,933, Universal
GoldenEye, $352,194,034, MGM
Pocahontas, $346,079,773, Walt Disney Pictures
film.gross.detail: Worldwide gross rather than domestic. The table's column header reads Rank, Title, Distributor, Worldwide gross, and the sentence above it calls the entries the top ten films released this year by worldwide gross, so header and text agree. Batman Forever was sixth at $336,529,144 for Warner Bros., Seven seventh at $327,311,859 for New Line, Casper eighth at $287,928,194 and Waterworld ninth at $264,218,220, both Universal, and Jumanji tenth at $262,797,249 for Sony and TriStar. A note inside the table's wikitext says the Toy Story figure covers its initial theatrical run and excludes later re-releases, and a capitalised editors' warning on the same row asks that the lifetime gross not be substituted.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.value: Braveheart, produced by Mel Gibson, Bruce Davey and Alan Ladd Jr.
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded the following spring at the 68th Academy Awards, hosted by Whoopi Goldberg at the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion in Los Angeles. Braveheart led the field with ten nominations and won five awards including Best Director for Gibson, and the ceremony page calls it the ninth film to win Best Picture with no acting nominations. Apollo 13 was second with nine nominations, and Babe and Sense and Sensibility had seven each. The other Best Picture nominees were Apollo 13, Babe, Il Postino: The Postman and Sense and Sensibility. Quincy Jones produced the telecast, which ran three hours and 39 minutes on ABC and drew 44.81 million viewers and 30.48 percent of households, both down on the previous ceremony.

film.acting_awards.label: Acting Oscars
value: Best Actor, Nicolas Cage, Leaving Las Vegas
Best Actress, Susan Sarandon, Dead Man Walking
Best Supporting Actor, Kevin Spacey, The Usual Suspects
Best Supporting Actress, Mira Sorvino, Mighty Aphrodite
film.acting_awards.detail: The ceremony page says this was the first year since the 42nd Academy Awards that none of the acting winners appeared in a Best Picture nominee, and that Sorvino was the second actress in a row to take Supporting Actress for a film directed by Woody Allen. Christopher McQuarrie won original screenplay for The Usual Suspects and Emma Thompson adapted screenplay for Sense and Sensibility, which the page says made her the first person to win Oscars for both acting and writing. Alan Menken shared Best Original Song for Colors of the Wind from Pocahontas. John Lasseter took a Special Achievement Award for leading the Pixar team on Toy Story. The film page's awards table gives the Golden Globe for drama to Sense and Sensibility and for comedy or musical to Babe, and the BAFTA award for Best Film to Sense and Sensibility and Best Director to Michael Radford.

film.world_cinema.label: Nominated for Best Foreign Language Film
value: Antonia's Line, the Netherlands, in Dutch, directed by Marleen Gorris, the winner
All Things Fair, Sweden, in Swedish, directed by Bo Widerberg
Dust of Life, Algeria, in French, directed by Rachid Bouchareb
O Quatrilho, Brazil, in Portuguese and Italian, directed by Fabio Barreto
The Star Maker, Italy, in Italian, directed by Giuseppe Tornatore
film.world_cinema.detail: The ceremony page states each film's country, language and director in this category. Il Postino: The Postman, an Italian production, was nominated for Best Picture instead and won Best Original Score for Luis Bacalov, and its lead Massimo Troisi was nominated for Best Actor after his death. None of the cached pages carries the Cannes, Venice or Berlin prizes for the year, so no festival winner is named here.

film.releases.label: Releases and studio changes
value: Crimson Tide, May 12, which the film page says opened the summer season
Die Hard with a Vengeance, May 19
Braveheart, May 24, directed by and starring Mel Gibson
Batman Forever, June 16, with the highest opening weekend to date at $52.8 million
Pocahontas, June 23, Walt Disney Pictures' 33rd feature
Apollo 13, June 30, directed by Ron Howard
GoldenEye, November 17, the James Bond series resuming after six years with Pierce Brosnan
Toy Story, November 22, the first feature-length film made entirely with computer-generated imagery
film.releases.detail: Pocahontas had premiered on June 10 in Central Park in New York City to an audience of 100,000 with free admission, which the film page calls the largest premiere ever for a film. Batman Forever passed Jurassic Park's opening weekend record, and the page says the Batman films became the fifth franchise to gross $1 billion. Matsushita sold 80 percent of MCA, which owned Universal Pictures, to Seagram for $7 billion on April 10. Carolco Pictures filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in November. Lars von Trier and Thomas Vinterberg announced the Dogme 95 movement in Paris on March 13. Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge was released in India this year.

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre, at an average ticket price of $4.35, and more and more often in one outside the United States. The film page says markets beyond the United States and Canada accounted for 41 percent of a film's total revenue and had outperformed the domestic box office for the first time the year before.
film.how_people_watched.detail: None of the cached pages says anything about tape rental, laser disc or a television premiere, so this fact claims nothing about home viewing. The page does say that the average cost of making and marketing a film had doubled since 1990 to reach $50.4 million, that first-quarter box-office revenue ran about $90 million below the same period the year before, and that Waterworld was the most expensive film made to that point.

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, season starting autumn 1995
value: ER, NBC, 22.0 rating
Seinfeld, NBC, 21.2
Friends, NBC, 18.7
Caroline in the City, NBC, 18.0
Monday Night Football, ABC, 17.1
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season, so this ranking covers the season that opened in the autumn and ran into the following spring. NBC held the top four places. The Single Guy was sixth on 16.7 for NBC, Home Improvement seventh on 16.1 for ABC, Boston Common eighth on 15.6 for NBC, 60 Minutes ninth on 14.2 for CBS and NYPD Blue tenth on 14.1 for ABC. 20/20 and Frasier tied for eleventh on 13.6.

tv.new_networks.label: Two new broadcast networks launch
tv.new_networks.value: The WB launched on January 11 and the United Paramount Network launched on January 16 with a two-hour premiere of Star Trek: Voyager
tv.new_networks.detail: The WB was a joint venture of Warner Bros. Television and Tribune Broadcasting under the chief executive Jamie Kellner, reached around 70 affiliates, and was also carried to cable and satellite providers through the WGN-TV superstation feed where no station was available. Its launch comedies were The Wayans Bros., The Parent 'Hood, Unhappily Ever After and Muscle. Kids' WB debuted on September 9 anchored by Animaniacs, which moved over from Fox Kids, and UPN Kids launched on September 10. Tribune bought a 12.5 percent limited partnership interest in The WB for $12 million on August 17. The Walt Disney Company announced on July 31 that it would acquire and merge with Capital Cities/ABC, and Westinghouse acquired CBS during the year after taking on CBS affiliations in Boston and Baltimore on January 2.

tv.simpson_verdict.label: O. J. Simpson verdict
tv.simpson_verdict.value: More than 150 million people watched the jury acquit him of murdering Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman
tv.simpson_verdict.detail: Live broadcasts of the trial had begun on January 24 and partly pre-empted network daytime programming for nine months. The television page says the verdict was met with both praise and criticism. During the trial on June 15 Simpson tried on gloves the prosecution presented as the killer's and they appeared too tight, and his lawyer Johnnie Cochran told the court that if it doesn't fit, you must acquit.

tv.premieres.label: Programs that debuted
value: Cybill, CBS, January 2
The Wayans Bros., The WB, January 11
Hercules: The Legendary Journeys, syndication, January 16
Star Trek: Voyager, UPN, January 16
NewsRadio, NBC, March 21
Sliders, Fox, March 22
The Outer Limits, Showtime, March 26
Xena: Warrior Princess, syndication, September 4
WCW Monday Nitro, TNT, September 4
Pinky and the Brain, Kids' WB, September 9
The Drew Carey Show, ABC, September 13
Murder One, ABC, September 19
Caroline in the City, NBC, September 21
JAG, NBC, September 23
Mad TV, Fox, October 14
Goosebumps, Fox Kids, October 27
tv.premieres.detail: The television page's premiere table gives each date and network. Its events table adds that What a Cartoon! launched simultaneously on TBS, TNT and Cartoon Network on February 20, opening with The Powerpuff Girls in Meat Fuzzy Lumpkins, and that Cartoon Network let viewers vote by telephone for their favourite short in a three-hour marathon on December 31. WCW Monday Nitro came from the Mall of America in Minneapolis. Seinfeld broadcast its 100th episode on February 2, and Frasier brought Ted Danson back as Sam Malone from Cheers on February 21.

tv.internet_broadcast.label: First television broadcast over the internet
tv.internet_broadcast.value: ROX and Computer Chronicles were sent out over the internet, which the television page calls the first internet broadcasts in the history of television
tv.internet_broadcast.detail: The same page dates the same claim twice and disagrees with itself: an April 18 entry says ROX became the first television series distributed via internet, while the November 20 entry makes the broader claim for both programs and carries an editors' note pointing readers to the talk page. Neither entry names a viewer count or a technology, so this fact states none.

music.hot100_year_end.label: Year-end Hot 100 singles
value: Gangsta's Paradise, Coolio featuring L.V.
Waterfalls, TLC
Creep, TLC
Kiss from a Rose, Seal
On Bended Knee, Boyz II Men
music.hot100_year_end.detail: From the Year in Music edition of Billboard dated December 23. The chart page says Gangsta's Paradise spent twelve weeks in the top two of the Hot 100 and three of them at number one. Boyz II Men, Brandy and The Notorious B.I.G. tied for the most songs on the year-end chart with four each, and all four of Brandy's came from her debut album. Real McCoy placed three, two of them inside the top forty. Hootie and the Blowfish put Hold My Hand, Let Her Cry and Only Wanna Be with You in the top forty. Michael Jackson was 21st with You Are Not Alone.

music.listening_format.label: How people listened
music.listening_format.value: A four-and-a-half hour broadcast that any station with a satellite receiver could pick up and carry. Eddie Vedder hosted Self-Pollution Radio on January 8 with live performances by Pearl Jam, Soundgarden and Mudhoney.
music.listening_format.detail: The cached pages carry no sales figure for records, tapes or compact discs this year, so this fact states none. What they do carry about format is what a catalogue reissue meant by now: The Offspring put their debut album, first released in 1989, on compact disc for the first time on November 21. Yo! MTV Raps ended on August 17 with a freestyle session, and Kiss played MTV Unplugged on August 9 with Peter Criss and Ace Frehley rejoining the lineup.

music.recordings.label: Albums released
value: The Bends, Radiohead, March 13
Post, Bjork, June 13
HIStory, Michael Jackson, June 20
(What's the Story) Morning Glory?, Oasis, October 2
Insomniac, Green Day, October 10
Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness, The Smashing Pumpkins, October 24
music.recordings.detail: The music page's aggregate ranking of the year's highest-rated albums, compiled from over 33,000 greatest-album charts, puts The Bends first, Morning Glory? second and Mellon Collie third, followed by Pulp's Different Class, Alanis Morissette's Jagged Little Pill and Post. The ranking's compilers state their results as accurate at a date years later, which is why no such date appears here. The page calls HIStory Jackson's first double album and gives its sales as 35 million copies, which it also expresses as 70 million. Elastica released Elastica on March 13, Celine Dion released D'eux on March 30, Rancid released ...And Out Come the Wolves on August 22 and dc Talk released Jesus Freak on November 21. The Beatles put out Free as a Bird on December 4, their first new single in over 20 years.

music.eurovision.label: Eurovision Song Contest
music.eurovision.value: The Irish-Norwegian band Secret Garden won the 40th contest for Norway with Nocturne, at the Point Theatre in Dublin
music.eurovision.detail: The music page calls it the last contest with only one host for many years. The 24th OTI Festival, at the Anfiteatro Jose Asuncion Flores in San Bernardino, Paraguay on November 11, was won by Eres mi debilidad, written by Alejandro Abad and performed by Marcos Llunas for Spain. Portishead's Dummy won the Mercury Music Prize.

music.tupac.label: Tupac Shakur records from prison and leaves it
music.tupac.value: Me Against the World was released on March 14 and made him the first male solo artist with a number one album on the Billboard 200 while in prison, and he was released on October 11 on $1.4 million bail posted by Suge Knight
music.tupac.detail: The music page says the album stayed at the top of the chart for four weeks, that he had been sentenced on February 7 to between one and a half and four and a half years on a sexual abuse charge, that he married Keisha Morris inside Clinton Correctional Facility on April 29, and that he signed a three-album deal with Knight's Death Row Records in return for the bail. Time Warner agreed on September 27 to sell back its 50 percent share of Interscope Records after criticism of the lyrics of the label's rap artists.

music.hall_of_fame.label: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame opens
music.hall_of_fame.value: The museum was dedicated in downtown Cleveland, in a building designed by I. M. Pei
music.hall_of_fame.detail: The music page dates the opening to the same day and gives no attendance or cost.

tech.windows_95.label: Windows 95
tech.windows_95.value: Microsoft released it to the public
tech.windows_95.detail: Both cached year pages carry the release and neither gives a sales figure or a price. The US year page's citation is a retrospective article about the hysteria over the launch.

tech.web_use.label: The internet passes into private hands
tech.web_use.value: The United States government stopped funding NSFNET, which made the internet a wholly privatized system
tech.web_use.detail: Prodigy had begun offering its subscribers access to the World Wide Web on January 27, which the science page cites to a report of the service's quick growth from it. Neither the science page nor either year page gives a count of users or hosts for the year, so no number is stated here.

tech.amazon.label: Amazon.com sells its first book
tech.amazon.value: The company, incorporated a year earlier by Jeff Bezos in Washington state as an online bookstore, sold Douglas Hofstadter's Fluid Concepts and Creative Analogies
tech.amazon.detail: The science page cites Amazon's own corporate timeline for the sale. It says nothing about revenue, staff or catalogue size, and no cached page mentions any other online shop opening this year.

tech.games.label: Video games
value: Sega Saturn, released in North America on May 11
PlayStation, Sony's console, released in the United States on September 9 and in Europe on September 29
Virtual Boy, Nintendo's 32-bit console, released in Japan on July 21 and discontinued on December 22
Chrono Trigger, Square, March 11, on the Super Nintendo
Full Throttle, LucasArts, April 30
Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island, Nintendo, August 5
Command & Conquer, Westwood Studios, August 31
Rayman, Ubisoft, September 9
tech.games.detail: The games page puts the Super Nintendo first in console sales at 3,518,000 or more worldwide, the PlayStation second at 3,100,000 and the Saturn third at 2,060,000 or more, and notes that the Nintendo Entertainment System was discontinued in North America on August 14. Virtua Fighter 2 took game of the year from Game Players and Gamest. The first Electronic Entertainment Expo was held in Los Angeles from May 11 to 13. Nintendo showed a playable Ultra 64 at its Space World exhibition in Japan on November 24 with thirteen games demonstrated and two of them playable. GameFAQs went up on the web on November 5 as an archive of game guides. BioWare and Remedy were founded during the year.

tech.web_tools.label: Software written this year for the web
value: The first Yahoo! Search interface, March 1
WikiWikiWeb, the first wiki software, loaded by Ward Cunningham in Oregon on March 25
The Java programming language, announced May 23
PHP, first version released by Rasmus Lerdorf on June 8
tech.web_tools.detail: The science page carries all four and dates them to the day. The US year page adds that Yahoo! was incorporated on March 2. The page's line about the share of web servers PHP would run years later is left out. Andy Harter's Virtual Network Computing is on the same page with no date at all, so it is not in this list.

tech.exoplanet.label: First planet found around an ordinary star
tech.exoplanet.value: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz of the University of Geneva announced the detection of 51 Pegasi b at the Observatoire de Haute-Provence, the first definitive extrasolar planet orbiting a main sequence star and the first hot Jupiter
tech.exoplanet.detail: Their paper appeared in Nature. The same page dates the announcement of the top quark to March 2 at Fermilab, the first sequencing of the genome of a free-living organism to the year without a day, and the discovery of the first brown dwarf, Teide 1, to the year as well.

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Unleaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31. Unchanged since the second stage of the increase Congress passed in 1989.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: Two American stories crowded out the rest: a bomb set off by an American in Oklahoma City, and a murder trial that pre-empted daytime television for months and ended in an acquittal watched live across the country. The new things to own were a games console made by a record company's parent and an operating system named after the year.

culture.million_man_march.label: Million Man March
culture.million_man_march.value: Black men gathered in Washington for a march conceived by the Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan
culture.million_man_march.detail: Both cached year pages carry the march and neither gives a crowd estimate, which was disputed at the time, so no figure is stated here.

culture.comic_strips.label: Two newspaper comic strips end
culture.comic_strips.value: Gary Larson's final The Far Side ran on January 1 and Bill Watterson's final original Calvin and Hobbes on December 31
culture.comic_strips.detail: The year page carries both, one on the first day of the year and one on the last, and the US year page repeats the second. Neither page gives a date for the Far Side strip beyond January 1.

culture.nobel_prizes.label: Nobel Prizes
value: Literature, Seamus Heaney
Peace, Joseph Rotblat and the Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs
Physics, Martin L. Perl and Frederick Reines
Chemistry, Paul J. Crutzen, Mario J. Molina and F. Sherwood Rowland
Medicine, Edward B. Lewis, Christiane Nusslein-Volhard and Eric Wieschaus
Economics, Robert Lucas Jr.
culture.nobel_prizes.detail: The year page gives no dates for any of them. The science page lists the same winners but names Rotblat alone for Peace, without the Pugwash Conferences. The Turing Award went to Manuel Blum, and Pierre and Marie Curie were enshrined in the Pantheon in Paris.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: Atlanta Braves beat the Cleveland Indians four games to two, with the pitcher Tom Glavine named series most valuable player
sports.world_series.detail: The television page dates the clinching game to October 28 and says the win made Atlanta the first major league team to win a championship for three different cities, the earlier two being Boston in 1914 and Milwaukee in 1957. ABC and NBC split coverage of the series between them under The Baseball Network, a revenue-sharing venture with Major League Baseball whose final broadcast this was, and Major League Baseball reached a new television deal with Fox and NBC on November 7 in which Fox paid $575 million over five years. The Seattle Mariners beat the California Angels 9 to 1 in a tie-breaker on October 2 for their first postseason place, after the Angels lost a 13-game lead in the division.

sports.ripken.label: Cal Ripken Jr. passes Lou Gehrig
sports.ripken.value: The Baltimore Orioles shortstop broke Gehrig's record of 2130 consecutive games played
sports.ripken.detail: The television page says a national audience watched on ESPN and viewers in Baltimore on HTS. The sports page names Ripken Associated Press Male Athlete of the Year, and Rebecca Lobo of college basketball Female Athlete of the Year.

sports.super_bowl.label: Super Bowl XXIX
sports.super_bowl.value: The San Francisco 49ers beat the San Diego Chargers 49 to 26 at Joe Robbie Stadium in front of 74,107, with the quarterback Steve Young named most valuable player
sports.super_bowl.detail: The US year page says the win made San Francisco the first National Football League franchise to take five Super Bowls. Nebraska had beaten Miami 24 to 17 in the Orange Bowl for the previous college season's national championship. The World League of American Football resumed after two years and Frankfurt Galaxy won the World Bowl 26 to 22 over the Amsterdam Admirals.

sports.rugby_world_cup.label: Rugby World Cup
sports.rugby_world_cup.value: South Africa beat New Zealand 15 to 12 in the final at home, decided by an extra-time drop goal from Joel Stransky
sports.rugby_world_cup.detail: The year page dates the tournament from May 25 to June 24 and says it was the Springboks' first appearance after World Rugby lifted their ban following the end of apartheid. The International Rugby Football Board lifted the century-old ban on professionalism on August 26. England won the 101st Five Nations Championship with a Grand Slam. A separate rugby league World Cup finished at Wembley Stadium on October 28, where Australia beat England 16 to 8 in front of 66,540.

sports.champions.label: Other championships
value: Stanley Cup, New Jersey Devils over the Detroit Red Wings, four games to none
NBA Finals, Houston Rockets over the Orlando Magic, four games to none
NCAA basketball, UCLA 89, Arkansas 78, the Bruins' first title in 20 years and eleventh overall
Premier League, Blackburn Rovers, denying Manchester United a third title in a row
Grey Cup, Baltimore Stallions 37, Calgary Stampeders 20, the first American-based winner
America's Cup, Team New Zealand's Black Magic over the San Diego defender, five races to none, which the US year page dates to May 14
sports.champions.detail: The sports page gives Jaromir Jagr of the Pittsburgh Penguins the Art Ross Trophy as leading scorer over the regular season and Eric Lindros of the Philadelphia Flyers the Hart Memorial Trophy. Ajax beat A.C. Milan 1 to 0 in the UEFA Champions League final in Vienna on May 24 and Norway beat Germany 2 to 0 in the FIFA Women's World Cup. Miguel Indurain won the Tour de France and Tony Rominger the Giro d'Italia. Ben Crenshaw took the Masters, Corey Pavin the US Open, John Daly the British Open and Steve Elkington the PGA Championship, with Greg Norman leading the money list at $1,654,959, and Europe won the Ryder Cup 14 and a half to 13 and a half. Pete Sampras won Wimbledon and the US Open and Steffi Graf three of the four women's majors. Stephen Hendry beat Nigel Bond 18 to 9 at the World Snooker Championship. Carlton won the 99th AFL premiership over Geelong. The two cached pages disagree on the beaten America's Cup defender: the sports page names Young America of the San Diego Yacht Club and the US year page names Stars and Stripes, so neither yacht is stated as fact here.

deaths.selena.label: Selena
deaths.selena.detail: Tejano singer-songwriter, shot by Yolanda Saldivar, her former personal assistant and fan club president, who had been fired for embezzling from the club. All the major American networks broke into programming with the news, and the music page says Hispanic listeners called the day Black Friday.

deaths.garcia.label: Jerry Garcia
deaths.garcia.detail: Guitarist of the Grateful Dead, of a heart attack at 53. The band's last show with him was at Soldier Field in Chicago on July 9, and the music page says deadheads gathered spontaneously in cities across the United States after his death.
